newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain, France want 5,000 troops in Zaire aid force.
newsitem.headline: Spain, France want 5,000 troops in Zaire aid force.

text.p: Spain and France want to send a multinational force of at least 5,000 troops in a relief effort to open humanitarian corridors for a million starving refugees in Zaire, a Foreign Ministry spokesman said on Wednesday.
French and Spanish leaders discussed the plan, which would require U.N. approval and the support of other countries, at a summit in Marseille on Monday and Tuesday.

France would send about 1,000 troops, Spain would send fewer than 1,000 and the two countries hoped the United States and other nations would contribute thousands more although none has yet committed itself to do so, the spokesman said.
"It is a concrete proposal by France and Spain. In the first phase, the troops will secure humanitarian corridors for food and medicine," said the spokesman, who asked not to be named.
A minimum of 5,000 soldiers would be needed for the operation to save refugees deprived of food by fighting between Zairean troops and Rwanda-backed Tutsi rebels, he added.
The Franco-Spanish initiative would have three phases in which the multinational force would be gradually replaced by African troops, Spain said.
